documentedRuntimeCapabilities.durationSemantics: The installed WeChat-maintained declarations describe duration as milliseconds for phase metrics; firstPaint, firstContentfulPaint and largestContentfulPaint are time points without duration.

revisedProbeRetests.source: user-provided local report after re-read and copy on the revised isolated probe
revisedProbeRetests.durationCaveat: The output showed no durations. Local review found observer entries are normalized to durationMs and then summarized again by code that previously read only duration, so timing values may have been lost by the probe. A regression test exposed this and the local formatter was fixed; a phone retest is required before concluding the underlying runtime omitted durations.
revisedProbeRetests.interpretation: The revised observer/read path captured 20 report rows on OPPO. The report intentionally redacts unrecognized names. The missing displayed durations are inconclusive because of a probe formatting defect; neither entry semantics nor FPS can be inferred from this output.

revisedProbeRetests.source: user-provided local report after the duration-formatting correction
revisedProbeRetests.interpretation: The duration-field correction is reflected in multiple rows. firstPaint, firstContentfulPaint and largestContentfulPaint are documented time points without duration; the route row still lacks a duration and remains unexplained. The report merged buffer and observer snapshots, and repeated output patterns could be duplicates. The probe now prefers the full buffer snapshot when nonempty; a phone run is needed to verify the cleaned output. Unrecognized render/interaction names are not interpreted as latency or FPS.

revisedProbeRetests.source: user-provided local report after being asked to run the isolated probe with the snapshot-source correction

This supports the buffer-snapshot selection change. The report does not embed its source revision, so the requested commit cannot be independently confirmed from the output. route still has no duration; firstPaint, firstContentfulPaint and largestContentfulPaint are time points without duration. systemTracingMenu.scope: User checked Developer Options > Debugging and did not find System Tracing; this records the checked path only, not every OEM entry point

fpsMeasurementResearch.status: SurfaceFlinger TimeStats ran on the connected Android 10 Huawei and reported an attributable WeChat AppBrandUI00 layer. A separate gfxinfo framestats query returns detailed timing rows from the WeChat appbrand0 process and identifies the same AppBrandUI00 window; the per-process reset command has now been verified on this Huawei. A 20-second manual FrameTimeline-only trace on OPPO PLJ110 overlapped a user-reported approximate five-second scroll and recorded 538 actual and expected frames on the named AppBrand host layer; all were classified On-time Present with no jank type. Gesture boundaries were not timestamped, no input tracks were included, and the embedded WebView was not isolated. This improves method-feasibility evidence but is not a scroll FPS result or QP05 acceptance evidence.

gpuRenderingFallback.method: Android Developer Options > Monitoring > Profile GPU Rendering/Profile HWUI Rendering > On screen as bars
gpuRenderingFallback.officialCapability: Official Android guidance describes a scrolling per-frame render-time histogram for a UI window, with a 16.67ms reference line for 60 FPS
gpuRenderingFallback.observed: User reports the histogram appeared over the WeChat mini-program device probe and refreshed during scrolling on DEVICE04; the attached screenshot shows the overlay over the probe page
gpuRenderingFallback.status: visual capture feasibility observed; numerical extraction and contract-grade per-segment statistics not validated
unverified: whether bar values can be extracted with adequate precision across repeated scrolling segments
whether the histogram's scale and app attribution can establish average FPS and detect app-attributable stalls over 100ms

surfaceFlingerTimeStats.method: ADB commands: adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --timestats -clear -enable; after one controlled scroll segment run adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --timestats -dump; always stop collection with adb shell dumpsys SurfaceFlinger --timestats -disable
surfaceFlingerTimeStats.officialGuidance: Android's Slow Sessions guide documents averageFPS and present-to-present histograms for SurfaceFlinger layers; Android dumpsys documentation also documents gfxinfo framestats as a detailed frame-timing source
surfaceFlingerTimeStats.histogramBoundary: Android 10 AOSP buckets include 98ms then 102ms and map deltas to the next configured boundary. A nonzero 102ms bucket can include values at or below 100ms, so it cannot by itself prove an exact >100ms stall; use exact frame timestamps or conservatively leave that segment unresolved.
surfaceFlingerTimeStats.officialScopeCaveat: The Android averageFPS procedure is presented in a games-only performance guide even though the command reports all tracked SurfaceFlinger layers. This project treats it only as a candidate until the Huawei output identifies an attributable foreground WeChat layer and the measurement is checked against the accepted thresholds.
surfaceFlingerTimeStats.captureChanges: -clear resets SurfaceFlinger TimeStats counters; -enable starts temporary frame-stat collection; -disable stops it. No app data, storage, network or persistent setting is changed.

latestFeasibilityCapture.timingWindowMismatch: The dump reports displayOnTime=33664ms and statsStart/statsEnd differ by 33 seconds, so the output does not establish an exact 15-second scroll segment.
latestFeasibilityCapture.interpretation: Confirms the Huawei accepts the command and exposes a WeChat AppBrandUI00 layer plus numeric per-layer statistics. It does not prove the 31.25 averageFPS or 350ms bucket came from a synchronized continuous scroll, nor identify the cause of that interval. Feasibility evidence only; do not pass or fail QP05 from this sample.

surfaceFlingerTimeStats.nextStep: The appbrand0 gfxinfo candidate below exposes recent frame timestamps and input-event columns, and its reset command is verified on this Android 10 process. Collect a synchronized short scroll sample and check whether frame rows with input timestamps align to the gesture. This does not upgrade the earlier SurfaceFlinger capture or count as QP05 evidence.
unverified: whether the sampled AppBrandUI00 intervals align with user scroll activity and can be bounded to fixed scroll segments
whether a long interval in this container layer can be attributed to an app-render stall rather than idle or surrounding activity
whether repeated per-segment SurfaceFlinger results satisfy QP05 sampling and attribution rules

gfxinfoFramestats.method: adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo com.tencent.mm:appbrand0 framestats
gfxinfoFramestats.resetCommand: adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo com.tencent.mm:appbrand0 reset
gfxinfoFramestats.officialGuidance: The cited AOSP guide describes framestats as nanosecond timestamps for the most recent 120 frames and documents reset as a way to constrain aggregate statistics to a particular animation; it says the framestats collection window is about two seconds.

appAttribution.interpretation: The main WeChat process was excluded because its ViewRoot was LauncherUI. The appbrand0 process returned one visible ViewRoot matching the resumed AppBrandUI00 page; appbrand1 returned no ViewRoot in the read-only check. Attribution is to the WeChat AppBrand host window, not an isolated WebView sublayer.

currentPreResetReadOnlySnapshot.scope: Cumulative process counters before reset; not bounded to a confirmed user gesture or to a short measurement interval.

postResetVerification.scope: Read after reset and before any requested scroll; no controlled gesture was synchronized to these frames.

preScrollReadOnlySnapshot.scope: Unsynchronized read immediately before a second reset; no user-confirmed gesture was in progress, so these frames are not assigned to an interaction.

controlledScrollWindowReset.scope: Second process-scoped reset immediately before the requested synchronized scroll sample; it resets transient gfxinfo counters only.

firstUserScrollAttempt.interpretation: The reset-relative aggregate spans about 240.6 seconds, not the requested five-second scroll. All ten returned recent frame rows have NewestInputEvent=0 and OldestInputEvent at the no-event sentinel. Therefore the capture cannot associate frames or gaps with the scroll, and no scroll FPS or app-attributable >100ms stall can be concluded. The process aggregate reports 0 janky frames, but this is not a segment result.

livePollScrollAttempt.interpretation: The user confirmed an approximate five-second scroll occurred during this 15.2-second live window. Polling saw no new frames through 5.331 seconds, then a rising count. The exact start/end were not timestamped; the reset-relative 203-frame/1-janky aggregate therefore cannot be converted to scroll FPS. All ten final rows had NewestInputEvent=0 and OldestInputEvent at the no-event sentinel, so the 165.3ms gap cannot be attributed to the scroll. No QP05 pass or fail is derived.

postCaptureForegroundCheck.scope: Read-only check after capture. The guarded automation issued no swipe because the mini-program page was no longer foreground; no phone setting was changed.

syntheticSwipeFeasibilitySample.interpretation: This confirms a successful, guarded five-second synthetic swipe and nonzero gfxinfo output from the visible AppBrand host ViewRoot. The aggregate frame count is not an FPS measure: the latest rows contain no input-event timestamps, gfxinfo does not isolate the embedded WebView compositor, and the command wall time includes ADB overhead. The zero janky count and percentiles are host-process feasibility data only. Do not infer FPS or QP05 pass/fail.

localTraceFeasibilitySample.perfettoServiceResult: Disconnected from the Perfetto traced service
localTraceFeasibilitySample.atraceLargeBufferResult: unable to start tracing: record-tgid Out of memory (12)
localTraceFeasibilitySample.interpretation: A seven-second local atrace overlapped a completed five-second synthetic swipe and retained input, AppBrand Choreographer and SurfaceFlinger vsync markers without buffer loss. It did not expose a separately attributable WebView presented-frame stream, so marker counts cannot be converted into application scroll FPS or QP05 pass/fail. Raw trace remains local and ignored by Git; no persistent phone setting was changed.

oppoFrameTimelineFeasibilitySample.source: official Perfetto FrameTimeline data source and official checksum-pinned Windows trace processor
oppoFrameTimelineFeasibilitySample.thirdTracePreparation: one downward swipe to return the diagnostic page toward the top before the five-second upward swipe
oppoFrameTimelineFeasibilitySample.interpretation: The Android 17 phone exposes FrameTimeline with a named AppBrand host layer and input slices. The only motion-related host frame burst spans about one second although the synthetic swipe command lasted five seconds. No separate WebView layer or actual product list with 200 heavy items was verified; the selected 120Hz refresh does not satisfy the 60Hz QP05 device condition. The trace processor also reported 975 systrace import failures. This establishes method feasibility only, not scroll FPS or QP05 pass/fail.

oppo60HzMethodCheck.secondTracePreparation: two short downward swipes before capture to return diagnostic page toward the top
oppo60HzMethodCheck.interpretation: The system display mode was 60 Hz and the named AppBrand host layer produced actual-frame records during a controlled diagnostic-page swipe. The first trace contained input but no AppBrand frames; the second has 152 host frames over 2.845 seconds and one 329.57 ms adjacent gap. The trace does not isolate the WebView, the complete five-second gesture, or the future 200-item product page. The gap cannot be attributed to an application stall, and the 948 import errors prevent claiming complete event capture. This is measurement-method feasibility only.

oppoFrameTimelineOnlyRetest.interpretation: The user reported an approximately five-second manual scroll completed during the 20-second FrameTimeline-only capture. Trace Processor found 538 actual and 538 expected frame records on the named AppBrand host layer spanning 10.079 seconds; all 538 actual records were On-time Present with jank_type=None and jank_severity_type=None. The maximum adjacent host-frame gap was 317.55ms. Because the gesture start/end were not timestamped, the gap cannot be attributed to the scroll; there were no input tracks and no separately verified embedded-WebView presented-frame stream. This is useful manual method-feasibility evidence on a diagnostic page, not an FPS result, app-stall attribution, product-page measurement or QP05 pass/fail.

limitations: The 1070-frame snapshot, later 1577-frame snapshot, and 3033-frame pre-reset snapshot are cumulative process summaries, not controlled interaction measurements.
The 115.81ms adjacent IntendedVsync interval came from ten recent rows without a synchronized gesture and cannot be treated as an app-attributable stall.
AOSP describes framestats as recent 120-frame timing data; it does not alone establish average FPS across the full product scroll segment or QP05's required repeated sample set.
The AppBrandUI00 host ViewRoot is attributable, but gfxinfo does not isolate the mini-program WebView renderer from the containing AppBrand UI.
A five-second synthetic ADB input swipe produced 93 host-process frames and 0 janky frames, but no input timestamps and no isolated WebView frame stream; this is not a scroll FPS result.
A local seven-second atrace retained input, AppBrand doFrame and SurfaceFlinger vsync markers without buffer loss but no separately attributable WebView presented frames.
The Android 17 OPPO FrameTimeline exposed an AppBrand host layer and frame records, but no separately verified WebView layer or contract-compliant 60Hz product scroll segment.
gfxinfoFramestats.nextStep: Keep R03 pending and do not repeat the same manual host trace: the user-reported approximate five-second scroll occurred during a 20-second FrameTimeline-only capture, but exact gesture boundaries were not timestamped and no separate WebView presented-frame stream was found. The isolated device probe now emits revision device-capability-v2-20261101-r1 and classifies the route duration field without exposing raw paths or values; local regression tests pass. Obtain one fresh OPPO report from that revision to establish the runtime field state. Continue resolving the iPhone frame-sampling path, minimum supported library and device groups. Do not infer FPS or QP05 from AppBrand host records. QP05 requires the actual product page, frozen 200-item content, device group, sampler and repeated timed segments; execute that contract only when the product page exists.
gfxinfoFramestats.scope: Local diagnostic queries, transient graphics-counter reset, guarded synthetic swipes and a short Android trace saved under Git-ignored .local/sp01-trace only; no cloud, app data, permissions or persistent phone setting was changed.

gpuProfileRetests.source: user-provided screenshot of the device capability report with GPU Rendering overlay; user confirmed the bars appeared over the probe and refreshed during scrolling
gpuProfileRetests.interpretation: The official per-frame histogram is visibly available over the WeChat WebView probe and refreshes during scrolling, establishing sampler visibility feasibility on this device. The capability report entries are not FPS; the screenshot does not provide raw numeric frame times, segment average FPS or app-attributed stalls over 100ms.

limitations: Selected display refresh settings are not measured display timing or FPS.
The probe reads its own page renderer, not a later formal product page's renderer.
Startup and first-render entries do not measure scroll FPS or button-to-visible-feedback latency.

The first four reports came from a version whose copy button did not refresh the page snapshot; preserve them as first-run evidence. The first revised OPPO report was affected by the duration formatter defect. A later report showed durations on 14 of 20 rows after buffer and observer snapshots had been merged. Following the snapshot-source correction, the next user-provided OPPO report had 10 rows and no repeated visible type/duration patterns; the report did not embed its source revision, so the exact executed build is unverified. The other three devices have not been rerun on the latest probe.

The meaning of unrecognized interaction/render entries, why the route row lacks duration, physical render latency, and FPS remain unverified. SurfaceFlinger TimeStats and appbrand0 gfxinfo are candidates only; synchronized scroll attribution still needs validation, and neither method is approved for contract sampling.
The backup Huawei's earlier reported base library 3.17.4 conflicts with the latest probe output 3.17.5; support baseline remains unresolved.
No minimum product base-library floor or device group is frozen by this evidence.
